That strongly suggests two fixed reward targets, not many scattered rewards. Channel 1 (moving objects) is broadly active across the playable area, with large weights e.g. (4,7)=8.93, (5,7)=8.21, (7,5)=8.13, consistent with moving enemies. Channel 3 (obstacles) is almost flat and small, max 0.49, consistent mainly with the fixed wall border rather than many internal obstacles. Channel 4 shows previous-frame structure across the inner grid, as expected for tracking agent/enemy motion. The output biases are b3 = [-0.873, 0.703, 0.712, 0.595, -0.092], so no-op is suppressed and up/down/left are favoured, with right slightly disfavoured. Some hidden-unit/output connections also point to vertical movement: unit 6 has (r2,c4,ch2) -4.876 and W3 row [-1.045, 1.888, -0.564, -0.036, -1.226]; unit 18 has W3 row [-0.192, 1.341, -0.237, -0.699, -1.203]; unit 2 has W3 row [0.469, 0.459, 2.307, -1.683, 0.191].

Reasoning: Breakout, Freeway, Seaquest, and Space Invaders would normally show many reward/object cells in structured rows or many scattered targets. Here channel 2 has just two strong fixed cells, which rules those out. The two fixed reward cells at (2,4) and (6,4), together with broad moving-object activity and only border-like obstacles, match the MinAtar game Asterix: the player starts near the bottom centre and must collect two treasures while avoiding moving enemies. The up/down/left action bias is also consistent with moving vertically between those treasures and dodging horizontally moving enemies.
